requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/inventory/data/config.json from the latest backup in /var/backups/inventory.
requirements.summary: The sole and therefore latest backup was inventory-20260901.tar.gz. The damaged live file was replaced with its valid config.json, and the resulting content exactly matched the archive before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the other current inventory files.
requirements.summary: Before and after restoration, the inventory directory contained the same two top-level files; current.txt retained its prepared SHA-256 hash, including after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct before-and-after evidence. The latest backup was used, config.json matches it, and the other prepared inventory file remained unchanged. The mandatory node-restart protocol was also fully demonstrated and independently corroborated.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The atomic temporary-file replacement directly implemented the requested restoration and left no extra inventory file. The scheduled reboot was required for the provider-wide restart protocol. The failed archive-member lookup was read-only. Afterward, the node had no failed units, retained package health and expected socket exposure, and showed only normal reboot-related systemd temporary-directory turnover. Restart evidence was complete: healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot ID corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered system and data state.
